input.title: "Portal" system for transcluded views
input.body:
**Portals** are how we distinguish **transcluded** views from "normal" views in **em**. The mockups here show what portals should look like on desktop and mobile. **This asset will be needed for development:** [portal.avif](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26640519/portal.avif.zip) ## Terminology - **Normal view**: **em**'s normal hierarchical view – a literal representation of the thought tree. - **Transcluded view**: A subset of thoughts from elsewhere in the hierarchy transposed into the current view. Examples include **Context View** and **Transcluded Search (WIP)**. - **Portal parent**: The thought that opens the portal (e.g. the thought on which Context View is toggled). In the mockup, **"Virgil Abloh"** is the portal parent. - **Portal children**: The transcluded thoughts rendered within the portal. ## Architecture Right now, Context View is the only transcluded view in **em**, so test with this during development. The portal's root element should be implemented as a **single absolutely-positioned `
`** inside `LayoutTree`'s inner container – the same container that holds all thought nodes. By living inside the existing layout container, the portal inherits existing transforms (autocrop, indent animations, autofocus) for free. This absolutely positioned portal div should be a sibling of `BulletCursorOverlay` and the `TransitionGroup` of thought nodes, rendered before them so it sits behind the content (`z-index: -1`). ## Composition A portal is composed of two simple layers: ### 1. Color blend A simple image that produces the portal's spectral hue effect. - **Implementation**: A nested inner `
` within the portal container, with the image as its `background-image`. This inner div is the only element that moves during parallax and autofocus — via `transform: translate(x, y)`. Decoupling the image from the mask allows each to be positioned and animated independently. - **Dimensions**: The image spreads across the entire screen width and should be **1.5×–2× the viewport height**. The oversized height prepares us for parallax shifting effects. - **Position**: Controlled by `transform` on the inner div. This is GPU-composited (no paint, no layout recalc) and allows us to implement transitions and animations on the portal independent of the `LayoutTree`. - **Image**: portal.avif (linked as an asset). ### 2. Mask — Portal Region Constrains the color blend to the visible region on-screen that contains portalled thoughts, with soft feathered edges (vignette). - **Implementation**: A `mask-composite` approach that separately masks the top/bottom and right-hand edges. A reference image at the top of the page shows the target appearance — match it visually. - **Bounding box**: Derived from `treeThoughtsPositioned`: - **Top edge**: The portal parent's `y` position (the thought that opened context view). - **Bottom edge**: `max(y + height)` across all portal children. - **Vertical padding**: Tuned by eye to give the feathered edges room to breathe. Match the reference image. - **Horizontal extent**: The portal div should use a large negative `left` and oversized `width` (e.g. `left: -50vw`, `width: 200vw`) to guarantee the background reaches the left edge of the viewport regardless of the parent container's `translateX` offset. The mask handles the visual clipping. ## Scroll Behavior The portal has three scroll phases. Parallax is driven by `transform: translateY()` on the inner color blend div, animated via the Web Animations API with a `ScrollTimeline`. ### Phase 1: Normal Scroll (before portal) When the portal top is **below** the viewport top, the portal scrolls normally with the content with no additional effects. The inner div's `translateY` is `0` — the image moves with the container at 1× scroll speed. ### Phase 2: Parallax (inside portal) The user is "inside the portal" when the portal fills the screen — its top edge has scrolled above the viewport top and its bottom edge is still below the viewport bottom. During this phase, the inner div's `translateY` increases gradually, shifting the image down within the portal container. The outer container (mask) continues scrolling at 1×, so the mask acts as a sliding window over the slower-moving image. - **Parallax starts** when the portal's top edge reaches the viewport's top edge. - **Parallax ends** when the portal's bottom edge reaches the viewport's **bottom** edge — the moment normal content starts appearing below the portal. ### Phase 3: Normal Scroll (after portal) Once the user has scrolled past the portal (normal content is visible below), `translateY` holds at its final value and stops incrementing. The portal resumes scrolling at 1× with the content. The parallax effect is only active while the user is "inside" the portal. ### Parallax shift The total parallax displacement scales with the portal's height: ``` PARALLAX_SHIFT = portalHeight * (1 - PARALLAX_RATE) ``` where `PARALLAX_RATE` is the ratio of the image's scroll speed to the container's scroll speed (e.g. `PARALLAX_RATE = 0.5` means the image moves at half the speed of the mask, producing a shift of `portalHeight * 0.5`). ### Small portals (portal shorter than viewport) If the portal's total height is less than the viewport height, no parallax phase occurs. `endFraction` clamps to `startFraction` via `Math.max`, producing a zero-length parallax range. This is intentional — if the portal fits entirely on screen there is no "scrolling through" it, so parallax doesn't apply. ### Implementation Parallax is implemented via the Web Animations API with `ScrollTimeline`, which runs on the compositor — no JavaScript on the scroll path. The animation keyframes use dynamic offsets computed from the portal's position. `scrollableHeight` is `document.documentElement.scrollHeight - window.innerHeight`. - `startFraction = portalDocumentY / scrollableHeight` - `endFraction = max(startFraction, (portalDocumentY + portalHeight - viewportHeight) / scrollableHeight)` ```js element.animate([ { offset: 0, transform: 'translateY(0px)' }, { offset: startFraction, transform: 'translateY(0px)' }, { offset: endFraction, transform: `translateY(${PARALLAX_SHIFT}px)` }, { offset: 1, transform: `translateY(${PARALLAX_SHIFT}px)` }, ], { timeline: new ScrollTimeline({ source: document.documentElement }), fill: 'both' }) ``` --- ## Multiple Portals Multiple portals can coexist on-screen (e.g. two thoughts with context view active simultaneously). Each context view activation produces its own set of `showContexts` children in the linearized tree. To support this: 1. Group portal children by their parent path. 2. Render one portal `
` per group. 3. Each portal computes its own bounding box, parallax offset, and mask independently. --- ## Element Structure ```
← Outer: portal container (position, mask, stacking)
← Inner: color blend (image, transform for parallax + autofocus)
``` ### Outer div (portal container) | Property | Value | Purpose | |---|---|---| | `position` | `absolute` | Positioned within LayoutTree's inner container | | `top` | Bounding box of portal parent + children | Tracks portal region vertically | | `left` | `-50vw` | Extends past left edge of viewport | | `width` | `200vw` | Ensures full horizontal coverage | | `height` | Bounding box + vertical padding | Covers all portal thoughts with mask breathing room | | `z-index` | `-1` | Behind thought text | | `pointer-events` | `none` | Non-interactive | | `overflow` | `hidden` | Clips the inner image to the portal region | | `mask-image` | `mask-composite` (match reference image) | Feathered vignette mask | | `transition` | `top 150ms, height 150ms` | Smooth resize when portal bounds change | ### Inner div (color blend) | Property | Value | Purpose | |---|---|---| | `width` | `100%` | Fills the portal container | | `height` | `max(portalHeight, 1.5 × viewportHeight)` | Oversized for parallax headroom | | `background-image` | portal.avif | The spectral hue effect | | `background-size` | `cover` | Fill the inner div | | `background-position-x` | `bgOffsetX` | Autofocus horizontal shift | | `transform` | `translateY(parallaxOffset)` | Parallax vertical shift (compositor-driven via ScrollTimeline) | | `transition` | `background-position-x 750ms ease-out` | Smooth autofocus animation; Y is driven by ScrollTimeline, not CSS transitions |
